p.seg: Chapter on Clarifying the Purpose and Meaning
Zhòng Ní 仲尼 was at home,
Zēng Zǐ 曾子 was in attendance.
The Master said:
"The former kings possessed supreme virtue and essential ways
with which to harmonize the world,
and the people were thereby harmonious and amicable,
with no resentment between superiors and inferiors.
Do you know this?"
Zēng Zǐ 曾子 rose from his mat and said:
"Cān 參 is not intelligent;
how could I be sufficient to know this?"
The Master said:
"Filial piety is the root of virtue,
the origin from which instruction arises.
Return to your seat;
I will tell you.
Your body, hair, and skin
are received from your parents.
Not daring to damage or injure them
is the beginning of filial piety.
Establishing yourself in life and practicing the Way,
making your name known to later generations,
thereby bringing glory to your parents,
is the end of filial piety."
"Filial piety begins with serving one's parents,
continues with serving one's ruler,
It begins with serving one's parents,
continues with serving one's lord,
and ends with establishing oneself.
The "Major Odes" say:
"Never forget your ancestors.
Cultivate their virtue."
"Chapter on the Son of Heaven"
The Master said:
"One who loves their parents does not dare to hate others;
one who respects their parents does not dare to be rude to others.
Loving and respecting are fully expressed in serving one's parents,
and virtuous teachings extend to the common people,
providing a model for the four seas;
this is the filial piety of the Son of Heaven.
The "Punishments of Fu" says:
'When one person is blessed,
the myriad people rely on it.'"
"Chapter on the Lords"
Not arrogant when in a high position,
lofty yet not dangerous.
Regulating expenditures and being careful with measures,
full yet not overflowing.
Lofty yet not dangerous
is how one can long preserve nobility.
Full yet not overflowing
is how one can long preserve wealth.
Fù guì bù lí qí shēn,
and then he can protect his state altars,
and harmonize his people.
This is the filial piety of the feudal lords.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Cautious, cautious,
as if facing a deep abyss,
as if treading on thin ice."
*Chapter on High Officials and Great Officers*
He dares not wear clothing that is not the prescribed attire of the former kings;
bù gǎn fú,
he dares not speak words that are not the prescribed sayings of the former kings;
bù gǎn dào,
he dares not perform deeds that are not the virtuous conduct of the former kings.
bù gǎn xíng.
Therefore, he does not speak what is not in accordance with the law;
he does not act contrary to the proper way.
His mouth has no faulty words,
his person has no faulty actions,
his words fill the world without verbal faults,
his actions fill the world without resentment or hatred.
When these three are complete,
then he can guard his ancestral temple.
This is the filial piety of high officials and great officers.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"From morning to night unremitting,
serving one person."
"The Scholar Chapter"
He draws from serving his father to serve his mother
and his love is the same;
he draws from serving his father to serve his ruler
and his respect is the same.
Therefore, from the mother he takes love,
and from the ruler he takes respect,
the one who embodies both is the father.
Therefore, if one serves the ruler with filial piety, then he is loyal;
if one serves his elders with respect, then he is obedient.
If loyalty and obedience are not lost,
in serving his superiors,
then he can preserve his rank and position,
and maintain his sacrifices.
This is the filial piety of a scholar.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Rising early and retiring late,
do not disgrace those who gave you life."
"The Commoner Chapter"
Using the way of heaven,
distributing the benefits of the earth,
being careful in conduct and frugal in expenditure,
to nourish his parents,
this is the filial piety of a commoner.
Therefore, from the Son of Heaven to the commoner,
filial piety has no end,
As for worrying about not reaching it,
that has never happened.
"Chapter on the Three Powers"
Zēng Zǐ said:
"How great is filial piety!"
The Master said:
"Filial piety
is the constant of Heaven,
the righteousness of Earth,
and the conduct of the people.
When the people take the constant of Heaven and Earth as their model,
ér mín shì zé zhī,
then they understand the brightness of Heaven,
take advantage of the benefits of Earth,
and thereby bring harmony to the world.
Therefore, their teachings are achieved without strictness,
and their government is ordered without severity.
The former kings saw that teaching could transform the people,
therefore, they first led them with universal love,
and the people did not abandon their parents;
they presented them with virtue and righteousness,
and the people eagerly practiced them;
they first led them with respect and yielding,
and the people did not contend;
they guided them with ritual and music,
and the people were harmonious;
they showed them what to like and dislike,
and the people will know what is forbidden.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Grand is Shī Yǐn,
the people all look up to you."
*Chapter on Governing with Filial Piety*
The Master said:
"In ancient times, when the enlightened kings governed the world with filial piety,
they did not dare to neglect even the ministers of small states,
how much less then dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons?
Therefore, they gained the hearts of all nations,
to serve their former kings.
Those who govern a state do not dare to slight widowers and widows,
how much less then scholars and the common people?
Therefore, they gained the hearts of the hundred surnames,
to serve their former lords.
Those who govern a family do not dare to fail their male and female servants,
how much less then their wives and children?
Therefore, they gained the hearts of the people,
to serve their parents.
If this is so,
then when they are alive, their parents are at peace,
and when they are sacrificed to, the spirits enjoy the offering.
Therefore, the world is peaceful,
disasters do not occur,
and calamities do not arise.
Thus, the enlightened kings governed the world with filial piety in this way.
The *Book of Poetry* says:
"Having awakened to virtue and conduct,
the four states submitted to him."
*Shèng Zhì Zhāng* (Chapter on Sagely Governance)
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask, is there a virtue of the sage
that is greater than filial piety?"
The Master said:
"Of all that Heaven and Earth produce,
humanity is the most esteemed.
Of human conduct,
nothing is greater than filial piety;
of filial piety, nothing is greater than revering one's father;
of revering one's father, nothing is greater than according him the honors due to Heaven.
Thus, Zhōu Gōng was such a man.
In the past, Zhōu Gōng performed the suburban sacrifice to Hòujì
to match him with Heaven,
and in the Mingtang, he offered ancestral sacrifices to Wén Wáng
to match him with God.
Therefore, within the four seas,
each performed sacrifices according to their respective duties.
What virtue of the sage, then,
could be greater than filial piety?
Hence, being near one's parents in their lap,
day by day, one nourishes one's parents with increasing reverence.
The sage, through reverence, teaches respect;
through familial closeness, teaches love.
The sage's teachings are achieved without strictness,
and their government is well-ordered without severity.
What they rely on is the foundation.
The Way of father and son
is a matter of Heaven's nature,
and the righteousness of ruler and minister.
Parents give birth to their children,"
and there is no greater continuation.
The ruler personally oversees them,
and there is no greater depth of care.
Therefore, those who do not love their parents but love others
are called morally perverse,
and those who do not respect their parents but respect others
are called ritually perverse.
Using obedience to create rebelliousness
provides no standards for the people to follow.
This does not reside in goodness,
but entirely in inauspicious virtue.
Even if you obtain it,
the gentleman does not value it.
A gentleman is not like this;
his words are thoughtful and can be spoken,
his actions are thoughtful and can bring joy,
his moral righteousness is worthy of respect,
his deeds are worthy of emulation,
his appearance and demeanor are worthy of observation,
his advances and retreats are measured,
with which he approaches his people.
Therefore, his people fear and love him,
They model themselves upon these [examples],
and thus are able to perfect their virtuous teachings,
and implement their governmental orders.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"The virtuous man and princely person,
his deportment is without error."」
*Jì Xiào Xíng Zhāng* (Chapter on Recording Filial Conduct)
Zǐ Yuē (Confucius said):
"The way a filial son serves his parents is this:
In their daily life, he shows them utmost respect;
In nourishing them, he gives them utmost pleasure;
When they are ill, he shows them utmost concern;
When they die, he shows them utmost grief;
In sacrificing to them, he shows them utmost solemnity.
When these five are complete,
then one can truly serve one's parents.
One who serves his parents,
when in a high position, will not be arrogant;
when in a subordinate position, will not be rebellious;
when among the masses, will not be contentious.
To be arrogant when in a high position
leads to ruin;
to be rebellious when in a subordinate position
leads to punishment;
to be contentious when among the masses
leads to warfare.
If these three are not eliminated,
Even if one daily uses the nourishment of three sacrificial animals,
it would still be considered unfilial."
*Wǔ Xíng Zhāng* (Chapter on the Five Punishments)
The Master said:
"The categories of the five punishments number three thousand,
but no crime is greater than unfilial piety.
He who coerces the ruler has no superior;
he who is not a sage has no law;
he who is not filial has no kin.
These are the paths to great disorder."
*Guǎng Yào Dào Zhāng* (Chapter on Broad Essential Principles)
The Master said:
"In teaching the people to be affectionate and loving,
nothing is better than filial piety.
In teaching the people to be courteous and obedient,
nothing is better than fraternal respect.
In transforming customs and changing practices,
nothing is better than music.
In securing the ruler and governing the people,
nothing is better than ritual.
Ritual is,
simply reverence.
Therefore, if one reveres his father,
then the son is pleased;
if one reveres his elder brother,
then the younger brother is pleased;
Respect his lord,
then the ministers will be pleased.
Respect one person and ten thousand people will be pleased.
Those who are respected are few, but those who are pleased are many,
this is called the essential way."
"Extending Perfect Virtue" chapter.
Zǐ said:
"The gentleman's teaching is based on filial piety;
it is not that he goes to each family and is seen daily.
Teaching filial piety
is the means by which to respect all fathers in the world.
Teaching fraternal duty
is the means by which to respect all elder brothers in the world.
Teaching ministership
is the means by which to respect all lords in the world.
The *Book of Odes* says:
'A kind and gentle gentleman,
is the parent of the people.'
If not perfect virtue,
who could cause the people to be so compliant on such a large scale!"
"Extending Reputation" chapter.
Zǐ said:
"The gentleman serves his parents with filial piety,
therefore loyalty can be transferred to the lord.
He serves his elder brother with fraternal duty,
therefore obedience can be transferred to superiors.
Managing the household,
therefore its governance can be applied to officialdom.
Thus, conduct is cultivated within,
and one's reputation is established for later generations."
"Chapter on Remonstrance"
Zēngzǐ said:
"As for kindness and love, respect and reverence,
bringing comfort to one's parents, and spreading one's good name,
I have already heard the instructions on these.
May I venture to ask if obedience to one's father's orders
can be called filial piety?"
The Master said:
"What words are these!
What words are these!
In the past, the Son of Heaven had seven ministers who remonstrated with him,
and though he was without the Way, he did not lose his empire;
the feudal lords had five ministers who remonstrated with them,
and though they were without the Way, they did not lose their states;
the grand officers had three ministers who remonstrated with them,
and though they were without the Way, they did not lose their families;
gentlemen had friends who remonstrated with them,
and thus their persons did not depart from honorable reputation;
fathers had sons who remonstrated with them,
and thus their persons did not fall into unrighteousness.
Therefore, when faced with unrighteousness,
a son must not fail to remonstrate with his father,
and a minister must not fail to remonstrate with his ruler.
Therefore, one should contend when faced with unrighteousness.
To follow the orders of one's father,
how then can that be considered filial piety!"
*Gǎn yìng zhāng* (Chapter on Response)
The Master said:
"In ancient times, enlightened kings served their fathers with filial piety,
therefore they served Heaven with understanding.
They served their mothers with filial piety,
therefore they served Earth with discernment.
The elder and younger brothers were in harmony,
therefore those above and below were well-governed.
When Heaven and Earth are understood and discerned,
the spirits will be manifest.
Therefore, even the Son of Heaven must have someone he respects,
meaning he has a father; he must have someone who came before him,
meaning he has an elder brother.
In ancestral temples, show utmost respect,
not forgetting one's parents.
Cultivate oneself and be careful in conduct,
fearing to disgrace one's ancestors.
In ancestral temples, show utmost respect,
and the ghosts and spirits will appear.
The ultimate in filial piety and fraternal respect
extends to the spirits,
shines upon the four seas,
and leaves nothing untouched.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"From the west, from the east.
From the south, from the north.
There is no thought that does not submit."
*Shì Jūn Zhāng* (Chapter on Serving One's Lord)
The Master said:
"When a *jūnzǐ* serves his superior,
when advancing, he thinks of exhausting his loyalty;
when retreating, he thinks of amending his faults;
he assists and complies with his superior's good qualities;
he corrects and rescues his bad qualities.
Therefore, superiors and inferiors can be intimate with each other.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
'In my heart I love him,
how could I not speak of him?
In my heart I treasure him,
on what day shall I forget him?'"
*Sāng Qīn Zhāng* (Chapter on Mourning Parents)
The Master said:
"When a filial son mourns his parents,
his weeping is not prolonged,
his rites are without elegance,
his words are without refinement,
he feels uneasy wearing beautiful clothes,
he does not enjoy hearing music,
he does not relish eating delicious food—
this is the feeling of grief and sorrow.
Three days without food;
teaching the people not to harm life for the sake of death;
destruction does not eradicate essence;
this is the governance of the sage.
Mourning does not exceed three years, showing the people there is an end.
Make for them coffins, outer coffins, clothing, and shrouds, and then lift them;
arrange their *fǔ* and *guǐ* vessels, and grieve and mourn for them;
beat the breast and stamp the feet, weep and wail;
bid farewell with sorrow;
divine the location of their tomb
and peacefully lay them to rest;
build for them ancestral temples
so that ghosts may enjoy offerings;
perform spring and autumn sacrifices
to remember them in due season.
Serve them with love and respect when alive;
serve them with grief and sorrow when dead;
the foundation of the people's livelihood is thus exhausted;
the meaning of death and life is fully prepared;
the filial son's service to his parents is completed."
